children: India's largest integrated private toll roads and highways infrastructure developer, IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd, on Wednesday (September 9), reported an approximately 25% year-on-year increase in gross toll revenue to ₹807 crore in August 2026, compared with ₹646 crore in August 2025.

IRB MP Expressway recorded toll revenue of ₹172.1 crore in August 2026, up from ₹144.7 crore a year earlier. IRB Golconda Expressway reported revenue of ₹87.9 crore, compared with ₹73.7 crore in August 2025.
IRB Ahmedabad Vadodara Super Express Tollway posted toll revenue of ₹80.3 crore, against ₹69.1 crore a year earlier, while IRB Lalitpur Tollway reported ₹43.5 crore, up from ₹36.1 crore.
Among other assets, IRB Tumkur Chitradurga Tollway recorded ₹38.4 crore versus ₹34.9 crore, while Udaipur Tollway reported ₹28.8 crore compared with ₹26.3 crore in August 2025.

Three assets reported toll revenue in August 2026 for which there was no year-earlier comparison in the filing. IRB Harihara Corridors Tollway reported ₹41.7 crore, IRB Chandibhadra Tollway reported ₹20 crore, and Meerut Budaun Expressway reported ₹22.6 crore.

IRB Kota Tollway's toll revenue declined to ₹6.3 crore from ₹7.1 crore, while Hapur Moradabad Tollway revenue fell to ₹22.3 crore from ₹28.9 crore. Kishangarh Gulabpura Tollway revenue declined to ₹22.5 crore from ₹23 crore.

The company said the Project Special Purpose Vehicles for IRB Harihara Corridors and IRB Chandibhadra Tollway received the Appointed Date from the National Highways Authority of India, with toll collection commencing on January 23, 2026 and April 1, 2026, respectively. Toll collection for Meerut Budaun Expressway commenced on May 17, 2026.

IRB Group has a portfolio of 28 revenue-generating highway assets across 13 states, with approximately ₹94,000 crore in assets and around 1.5 million vehicle crossings daily, according to the filing. The group plans to expand its asset base to approximately ₹1.4 lakh crore by FY2029 through its asset churn strategy.

Amitabh Murarka, Deputy CEO, IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd, said, "Our strong toll revenue performance in August 2026 reflects the sustained traffic growth across our assets. The growth in traffic, coupled with the tariff revision implemented at the beginning of FY27, has further supported our revenue performance."

"With robust GDP growth indicating sustained economic activity, coupled with the onset of the festive season beginning with the Ganesh Festival, we expect the positive traffic momentum to continue. We remain well positioned to deliver stronger toll revenue growth in the coming months, further strengthening our overall growth momentum."
Shares of IRB Infrastructure Developers Limited ended at ₹19.07, down by ₹0.18, or 0.94%, on the BSE.

title: IRB Infrastructure Developers' toll revenue surges 25% to ₹807 crore in August
